rv.q: You get your money's worth in energy alone.
At Lifeline Theatre, it becomes something exhilarating.

This incredible ensemble effort has created what, 4+ months into the year, is easily the best show of 2026 so far: a show that could have been complicated and confusing instead hits every note and every emotion.
Loki absolutely blazes through its 150-minute running time and director Heather Currie and her cast are firing on all cylinders.
It’s smart, loud, heartfelt, and just strange enough to feel genuinely new - the sort of show you want to tell people about before it closes.
Meantime, if you're a fan of rock musicals, Norse mythology, or just kick-ass new storefront extravaganzas, Loki shouldn't be missed.
This epic, ambitious and brilliantly spectacular rock musical may be one of the best shows of the year.
Ultimately, Loki—The End of the World Tour is an ambitious and imaginative production embracing spectacle without losing sight of its emotional core.

cn.t: Critics hail this wildly imaginative rock musical as audacious and brilliant, praising its irresistible premise of Norse apocalypse as eternal arena concert and calling it a strong contender for year's best show.
